guarantees.claim: When SecMasking is false, unused_state_mask is driven to state_mask.
When SecMasking is true, state_init[0] = (state_in ^ add_state_in) ^ state_mask (masked data share) and state_init[1] = state_mask (mask share).
When SecMasking is false, key_init_cipher[0] is driven to key_init_q[0] ^ key_init_q[1], combining the two key shares into a single unmasked key.
When SecMasking is true, key_init_cipher is driven directly to key_init_q, forwarding both key shares.

assumptions.claim: In unmasked mode, key_init_q[0] and key_init_q[1] must together form the correct key (key = share0 ^ share1).
assumptions.risk: If the shares are incorrect, the cipher core will use the wrong key.

assumptions.claim: In masked mode, the downstream consumer of key_init_cipher must interpret it as two separate key shares, not as a combined key.
assumptions.risk: If the downstream logic expects a combined key, it will mishandle the secret, potentially breaking masking.

assumptions.claim: When SecMasking is true, state_in and add_state_in are not already masked; they are the plain intermediate values to be protected by the applied mask.
assumptions.risk: If these inputs are already masked, double masking will corrupt the AES computation.

assumptions.claim: In unmasked mode, state_init must be driven by another block; this chunk only ties off unused_state_mask.
assumptions.risk: If no other logic drives state_init, it will be X, causing functional failure.

assumptions.claim: unused_state_mask is not used as an active mask or data signal elsewhere; it exists only to suppress lint warnings.
assumptions.risk: If it is inadvertently used as a valid mask, the unmasked path could leak state_mask.

uncertain_points.claim: In unmasked state init path, state_init is not assigned; the drive must come from another generate block or instance.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven state_init leads to X values propagating into the cipher datapath.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_state_mask is intentionally named as unused; verify it is indeed unused and does not inadvertently fan out to any logic.
uncertain_points.risk: No functional risk if truly floating; otherwise could indicate a forgotten connection.

uncertain_points.claim: In unmasked key generation, only key_init_cipher[0] is assigned; key_init_cipher[1] may be left undriven if the vector has two elements.
uncertain_points.cond: SecMasking == 0 and key_init_cipher defined as a packed array of size 2
uncertain_points.risk: An undriven key share bit could inject X into the unmasked key path, breaking encryption.

uncertain_points.claim: state_in and add_state_in may already be masked before reaching this masking step; double masking must be ruled out by upstream logic.
uncertain_points.risk: Double application of mask share destroys correctness of masked AES S‑box results.
